explanation: A layer-0 unigram detector: the pole fires on the current token's string when that string is an atypical, non-ordinary-English piece of vocabulary - the bare word fragment 'be' (as in 'would-be', 'honeybees', 'remembe'), surname/name fragments (' Bi', 'Be', ' Bor', ' Bon', ' Don', ' Ferr', ' Brun'), Latinate/Greek technical roots (' Thermo', ' glyc', ' trache', ' diab', ' bacteri'), foreign words ('habe', 'gibt', ' Deutsch', 'degli') and code identifiers or digit runs ('artifactId', 'github', '19', '299') - while it is exactly zero on common word pieces ('ing', 'tion', 'ment'), on function words and on punctuation, and zero or weak on most ordinary English words (a minority such as 'face', 'body', 'name', 'given', 'food', 'social' fire at 0.3-0.8). Activation is a fixed function of the current token's embedding alone (identical at every position and context, hence retrospective with no lookahead), and within those classes membership is idiosyncratic - most fresh technical, foreign or code fragments stay silent - so the decisive predictor is the token string itself, with the sharpest contrast the bare fragment 'be' at the maximum 1.33 versus the ordinary word ' be' at exactly 0.
